title: What Are QBTS Stock Investors Overlooking?
detail:
What Are QBTS Stock Investors Overlooking?
Trefis Team

QBTS

RGTI

GOOG

Image from Pixabay

D-Wave Quantum (QBTS) reported revenue of $3.1 million for the second quarter of 2026, a figure essentially flat compared to a year earlier. This stagnation stands out given the $5.4 billion valuation investors have placed on the business, a price that appears to anticipate rapid growth. Underneath the top line, cloud subscriptions and professional services actually expanded at double-digit rates during the period. So why did D-Wave's revenue stand still?

D-Wave Booked Very Little From Selling Computers

The company generated little of its second-quarter revenue from actual quantum computer sales. Systems and other revenue totaled about $300,000 for the period, even though management prices a single annealing system between $20 million and $40 million.

The rest of the business actually grew. Subscriptions to D-Wave's quantum cloud service increased 50% from a year earlier, and professional services climbed by more than 18%. Because total revenue remained flat overall, falling systems revenue appears to have offset those gains.

Selling physical hardware simply takes time. During the second-quarter 2026 earnings call, management explained that system timing typically depends on site selection. Once a location is finalized, each machine must still be built, installed, and calibrated.

Looking over the latest twelve months, D-Wave's revenue performed worse than flat. Revenue fell 44%, mostly because first-quarter revenue dropped 81% from a year earlier. That is a stark contrast to its three-year average of 37.7% growth a year.

D-Wave's Adjusted EBITDA Loss Has Widened

D-Wave's costs increased during the quarter without a corresponding bump in revenue. D-Wave's adjusted EBITDA loss widened 85% from a year earlier, an expansion management attributed mostly to product development and sales staff expenses. Gross margin also dropped to 55.4% from 63.8% a year earlier, with management again pointing to personnel costs.

The stock has already taken a heavy hit. D-Wave shares lost 59% over the past twelve months, while the S&P 500 returned 17.0%. Despite that drop, the shares still trade at 434.9 times sales, compared to 3.1 for the S&P 500. This valuation likely assumes future revenue will eclipse today's baseline many times over.

D-Wave Expects A Bigger Fourth Quarter

The company does have orders in hand that have not yet converted into revenue. D-Wave's backlog reached $40.7 million on June 30, 2026, up 668% from a year earlier. Management expects about 57% of that backlog to become revenue within twelve months.

title: What Is Next For Rigetti Stock?
detail:
What Is Next For Rigetti Stock?
Trefis Team
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 6:57 AM PDT 3 min read
RGTI
^GSPC
IONQ
QBTS
IBM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Shares of Rigetti Computing (RGTI) have fallen 68% over the past twelve months, trailing the 17.0% return of the S&P 500. Despite this steep decline, the company retains a valuation of about $4.7 billion while losing about $0.2 billion over its last twelve months. Investors paying this premium appear to be betting on sales that have not arrived yet. Current market pricing appears to assume a sales volume many times larger than a handful of orders of this size. At the S&P 500's 3.1 times sales, a $4.7 billion value would need about $1.5 billion of yearly sales.

Rigetti Is Selling Quantum Computing Systems To Customers

The hardware maker is currently focused on selling quantum computing systems, and early buyers are stepping up. Its product is Novera, a system delivered directly to a customer's own site.

This strategy is beginning to register in the financial results. Rigetti recorded revenue of about $5.1 million for the second quarter of 2026, up from $1.8 million a year earlier. During an August 6, 2026 call, management noted that Novera sales drove the increase as older purchase orders converted into recognized revenue.

Corporations are driving much of this initial activity. Management noted that commercial organizations buying systems for their own sites accounted for most of the sales growth in the first half. Alongside corporate interest, the company also reported more demand for Novera from national labs and universities.

Rigetti's Orders Are Small Next To Its Value

Next to Rigetti's own sales, one major deal stands out: C-DAC has ordered a 108-qubit system for India at a price of $8.4 million. That single contract is worth more than all the revenue Rigetti reported for the second quarter. Management expects to recognize it as revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Compare an order of that size with the price investors are paying for the company. Rigetti stock trades at 350.1 times its sales over the past twelve months, compared with a multiple of 3.1 times for the S&P 500. Current market pricing appears to assume a sales volume many times larger than a handful of orders of this size, a reality that holds true even with shares trading 74.9% below their 52-week high.

Can Rigetti Deliver The 108-Qubit System On Schedule?

As of the August 6 call, Rigetti had not yet turned the C-DAC order into revenue. The transaction only clears that accounting threshold after the company installs the system and it passes performance acceptance testing. Management indicated that revenue will continue to fluctuate based on the timing of system deliveries, meaning one strong quarter says little about the next.

International Business Machines Corporation (IBM) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It

^GSPC

IBM (IBM) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this technology and consulting company have returned -6.6%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +2.4% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry, which IBM falls in, has gained 5%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, IBM is expected to post earnings of $2.87 per share, indicating a change of +8.3% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0.5% over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $12.33 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +6.4%. This estimate has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $13.2 indicates a change of +7% from what IBM is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +0.1%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, IBM is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

title: IBM Consulting Grew Profit 15% on Nearly Flat Sales. Can That Continue?
detail:
IBM Consulting Grew Profit 15% on Nearly Flat Sales. Can That Continue?
Habib Ur Rehman
Fri, October 9, 2026 at 9:05 AM PDT 3 min read
IBM
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM) produced a useful surprise inside its consulting business: second-quarter segment profit rose 15.1%, although revenue increased just 0.2%. Improving delivery economics can lift earnings, but repeated margin expansion becomes harder when sales barely move.

The July 22 results and quarterly filing showed $647 million of consulting segment profit on $5.327 billion of revenue. A year earlier, profit was $562 million. IBM attributed the improvement primarily to productivity actions, partly offset by investment in innovation.

IBM ranked ninth in our recent cybersecurity screen. See which security-focused alternatives ranked higher on analyst target upside than this diversified enterprise-technology company.

IBM Consulting Grew Profit 15% on Nearly Flat Sales. Can That Continue?

For illustration purposes only: work on a laptop.

Each margin point has a measurable payoff

At the reported revenue base, one percentage point of consulting margin represents $53.3 million of quarterly segment profit. A one-point retreat would absorb more than three-fifths of the quarter's $85 million year-over-year profit gain. This is a sensitivity calculation, not a forecast.

Consulting gross margin also improved, to 28.9% from 27.5%. That places part of the gain in the economics of delivering client work. Better utilization and more efficient delivery can preserve profit without requiring a surge in billings.

Our Amazon margin analysis puts a dollar value on similar segment-level efficiency gains and shows why the whole-company valuation still needs a separate test.

There is supporting demand evidence. Consulting signings increased 5% as reported, and the trailing book-to-bill ratio was 1.05. Those indicators could help sales resume growing. Their conversion depends on project timing and customer commitments; signings are management estimates rather than a standardized revenue measure.

A book-to-bill ratio just above one indicates that trailing signings modestly exceeded revenue, not that revenue is about to accelerate by the same percentage. Contract duration and the pace of work can separate bookings from sales for several quarters. Demand conversion matters because efficiency gains eventually become a tougher year-over-year comparison.

Better delivery economics need a durable customer base

A falling cost base can reward shareholders even before demand accelerates. The bear case is that further efficiency gains become harder to achieve, or customers retain some benefit through lower prices.

Repeating 15% profit growth with a flat margin would require roughly 15% revenue growth, far above this quarter's pace. With flat revenue, it would instead require the segment margin to rise from about 12.1% to 14.0%. These alternatives illustrate the burden of sustaining the profit growth rate; neither is management guidance.

International Business Machines Corporation IBM has launched IBM Ready for SAP SE SAP Solutions to help midsize and fast-growing businesses modernize their enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, improve productivity and support business growth.

Under the program, IBM will combine its industry expertise, fit-to-standard implementation approach and IBM Consulting Advantage, its artificial intelligence (AI)-powered consulting delivery platform, to accelerate the adoption of SAP Cloud ERP. The offering aims to simplify business processes, integrate enterprise data and help organizations manage their growing operations.

IBM helped Volumetric Building Companies reduce operational cycle times by 50% across purchasing, manufacturing and inventory processes after a three-month SAP Cloud ERP transformation. Meanwhile, the company also supported Second Nature Brands in integrating its acquired Voortman Bakery business into a common enterprise platform.

According to research from the IBM Institute for Business Value, 68% of enterprises consider accelerating ERP modernization important for improving operational efficiency and maintaining competitiveness. The findings highlight the growing importance of modern enterprise systems and reinforce the company's efforts to help businesses streamline operations, support growth and prepare for future AI applications.

How Are Competitors Advancing?

IBM faces competition from Microsoft Corporation MSFT and Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN. Microsoft is expanding its Dynamics 365 ERP software with AI tools to automate finance, supply chain and business operations. The company is developing AI agents that can analyze data and handle routine business tasks. Microsoft aims to help businesses automate workflows, track financial performance and manage supply chain activities through its connected ERP systems.

Amazon Web Services is helping businesses integrate AI tools with SAP ERP systems to automate business tasks. The company introduced tools helping AI agents securely access enterprise data and work across business applications. Amazon is expanding its cloud and AI services to help organizations modernize legacy systems, improve data management and streamline business operations.

IBM shares have lost 18.4% over the past year against the industry's growth of 167.6%.

title: IBM (IBM) Saw Mainframes Fall 42%. Is That Already Priced In at 18 Times Earnings?
detail:
IBM (IBM) Saw Mainframes Fall 42%. Is That Already Priced In at 18 Times Earnings?
Maham Fatima
Fri, October 9, 2026 at 6:29 AM PDT 4 min read
IBM
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Two halves of the same company just moved in opposite directions. International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) saw its IBM Z mainframe line fall 42% in fiscal Q2 2026, while distributed infrastructure, which covers Power and Storage, jumped 37%. Total revenue rose only 1% to $17.2 billion, and management updated its full-year outlook to 4% to 5% constant-currency growth.

IBM sells software (Red Hat, data tools, automation), consulting, and the infrastructure that runs big companies' systems. Software is its highest-margin segment, with a 32.2% segment profit margin. Whether the miss is a pothole or a warning depends less on the mainframe number than on what software does next, and on whether 18 times earnings already reflects it.

CrowdStrike (CRWD) Is Accelerating Again. Is 219 Times Earnings Too Far Ahead?
Margins Tell the Story

The moat shows up in the economics rather than the marketing. Software carried an 82.6% gross margin in the quarter, and its segment profit margin improved from 31.1% a year earlier. Red Hat, the open-source arm, grew 11%, and the data business grew 19%.

Even after the miss, the balance sheet showed $16,160 million of current deferred income (billed to clients, not yet counted as revenue), a sign the contract base hasn't evaporated. For investors looking past high-flying multiples, reviewing the best 52-week low technology stocks offers a look at beaten-down alternatives.

A Pause, Not a Collapse

Zoom out and the mainframe slump looks more like a pause than a collapse. Infrastructure revenue rose 1.9% across the first half even after falling 7% in the second quarter. Power and Storage ended the quarter with an order backlog (committed but undelivered orders) of nearly $500 million.

IBM has also kept spending on what comes next. Since the report, it unveiled a dual-architecture mainframe processor, designed to let companies run operating systems and applications on both IBM and Arm platforms. It also closed its purchase of HRL Laboratories, a research institution spanning quantum computing and advanced electronics, and plans to invest more than $10 billion in quantum over five years. None of that pays off soon, but it suggests the moat is holding rather than eroding.

Is Software the Real Problem?

The tougher question for bulls is software, the business that has to carry growth. It grew 5% in fiscal Q2, slower than the 7.9% pace across the first half, and Transaction Processing, one of its lines, shrank 8%. Consulting was flat at $5.3 billion. Free cash flow of $2.5 billion slipped $0.3 billion from a year earlier, and debt totals $62.0 billion after $10.5 billion of acquisitions this year.
